Each person's weights sum to 1 after normalizing. A color with weight $a$ can hold at most 31 people under load $C'$, and one with weight $b$ can hold at most 30. The total capacity is $44\cdot 31 + 22\cdot 30 = 2024 < 2025$, so the selector cannot keep every color within $C'$. This gives $C > 31/66$.

**Solution 3 ($992/2091 \approx 0.4744$) is also refuted.** It falls below the valid lower bound $992/2069 \approx 0.4795$ from Solution 2's construction. **Solution 2 ($992/2069$) is the closest, but it is not optimal.** Its identical-rows approach is the right framework, but it wastes one unit of capacity. In general, with identical rows and $m_j$ the number of people on color $j$ at load just below $C$, the constraints are $\sum m_j \le n-1$ and $\sum C/(m_j+1) \le 1$. So $C = 1/\min \sum_j \frac{1}{x_j}$ with $\sum x_j = n+k-1 = 2090$. Balancing gives 44 values of $x_j = 32$ and 22 values of $x_j = 31$. Then
$$\sum_j \frac{1}{x_j} = \frac{44}{32}+\frac{22}{31} = \frac{517}{248},$$
so the identical-rows value is $C = \frac{248}{517} \approx 0.47969$, which exceeds $992/2069 \approx 0.47946$.

As a sanity check, this formula gives $6/5$ for $n=4$, $k=2$, matching the value Solution 3 cites.
